subject: Mutual plan: SOC2/SIG gaps, DPA redline and retention choices
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Kane <oliver.kane@fortuna-bank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual plan: SOC2/SIG gaps, DPA redline and retention choices

Oliver — thanks for the call this morning. I captured the initial mutual action plan (attached MAP-v1.xlsx) and wanted to confirm next steps and owners so we can hit your Q4 pilot target. Key security/compliance gates we recommend placing into the MAP:

- SOC 2: target SOC 2 Type II evidence snapshot (scoped to inference runtime) — Redwood provides existing attestation and control mappings; we need confirmation of in-scope services from your compliance team.
- SIG/CAIQ: we'll deliver a completed SIG questionnaire and a focused CAIQ extract for your security team; your team asked for clarifications on three controls (networking, key management, logging).
- DPA: Kimberly has provided a redline; primary open items are data residency and subprocessor list.
- Data retention & residency: Fortuna asked for a 30/90/365 tiering proposal plus an EU-only residency option for regulated datasets. We propose EU residency (customer-managed VPC) for regulated data and a 90-day token retention for ephemeral inference metadata by default.

Proposed immediate actions (short mutual milestones):
- Today: Kimberly to circulate DPA redline (attached).
- Tue (48h): Security Qs — Redwood to deliver SIG/CAIQ clarifications and a short control mapping focused on key mgmt and audit logging (owner: Neha).
- Thu: Fortuna to confirm in-scope services for SOC 2 snapshot and indicate whether EU-residency is required for the pilot.

Can I confirm these owners & deadlines? If that works I’ll update the MAP and send a single tracker so we can gate approval decisions off clear acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
— Priyom
Sr. Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), DPA_redline_20260815.docx (docx)

From: Oliver Kane <oliver.kane@fortuna-bank.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@fortuna-bank.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 08:41:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Mutual plan: SOC2/SIG gaps, DPA redline and retention choices

Priyom — thanks for the summary. That aligns with our internal read. A few clarifications from Fortuna Security & Legal: 

- SOC 2: we only need controls for "inference" and key customer-facing APIs for the pilot; we can share the exact list by Thu.
- SIG: the three clarifications are critical — especially control AC-6 (privileged access) and KM-2 (key lifecycle). Please flag where Redwood’s hosted offering requires KMS or HSM integrations.
- DPA: legal prefers EU-residency for any data classified as PII for EU customers. Also, a retention choice: 90 days for logs, 30 days for prompts, 0 days for LLM-generated ephemeral outputs unless explicitly stored.

We approve the proposed owners. Please have Neha send the SIG clarifications and an example KMS diagram. Kimberly’s redline will be reviewed this afternoon and we’ll push any comments back by Thu EOD.

Oliver
Head of Security Operations
Fortuna Bank

Quoted below for context: 
> On Mon, 16 Aug 2026, Priyom Das wrote:
> > Oliver — thanks for the call this morning. I captured the initial mutual action plan (attached MAP-v1.xlsx) and wanted to confirm next steps and owners so we can hit your Q4 pilot target.

Attachment: Fortuna-reqs-summary.pdf (referenced)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Kane <oliver.kane@fortuna-bank.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DPA redline + quick notes on residency and escrow

Oliver / team — forwarding our redline (attached DPA_redline_20260815.docx). Highlights: 

1) Residency: we can offer EU-only processing under Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) for regulated datasets. We will add KMS integration language (support for external KMS + HSM attestations).
2) Retention: proposing the 90/30/0 tier you outlined, with an option to configure shorter windows for specific data classes via the Console.
3) Subprocessors: we included a narrow list and a 30-day notice for any changes; if Fortuna requires prior approval for changes to that list, flag here and we’ll evaluate.
4) Escrow / continuity: standard continuity commitments included; if you want source escrow we should list the trigger and timeframe — that typically requires FT negotiation.

Please see inline comments in the attached redline. If you confirm EU residency and the 90/30/0 retention model, we can mark those as satisfied acceptance criteria in the MAP and move SOC 2 scoping to evidence collection.

— Kimberly
Head of Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_redline_20260815.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: Mutual plan: SOC2/SIG gaps, DPA redline and retention choices

Kimberly / Priyom — confirmed. Fortuna will accept EU residency for regulated datasets and the 90/30/0 retention bands for the pilot. We have one ask: can Redwood provide a short runbook describing how a customer requests a retention change and the expected lead time for propagation to production (we need SLA for change time)?

If you can add that to the MAP and include the SIG clarifications (Neha) we’ll mark acceptance for the pilot and proceed to SOC 2 scoping. Final acceptance target: 2026-09-10 (internal sign-off).

Thanks — Aisha
Procurement & Vendor Risk
Fortuna Bank
